The loop header is not an array access and does not prove that the incoming payload is unallocated. The queue can receive either allocated or zero-length payloads, and the old block-entry projection incorrectly promoted the caller's possible state to a deterministic VBA249 failure.

A zero-length WebSocket payload can remain unallocated when it is copied through the BinaryMessage queue, but allocated payloads are also valid and the queue path is conditional. The UBound use is therefore possible rather than guaranteed; the old deterministic VBA249 projection was a false positive and the focused regression retains the lower-confidence VBA227 warning.

The For body cannot execute when LBound or UBound fails on an unallocated payload, so the indexed data(i) access is not itself a deterministic unallocated-array failure. The old block-level scan reported it without respecting the successful bound-query prerequisite.
